records.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create ONE polished biomedical editorial illustration for a professional genetics image-jigsaw game. Landscape 4:3, ideally 1600x1200. Crisp silhouettes, elegant dimensional scientific forms, restrained richly detailed illustration, white and ice-blue background. Palette navy #0c063f, royal blue #0043fd, cyan #00a9f2, muted teal, restrained amber accent. Design meaningful distinguishable biological shapes across a 4-column,3-row jigsaw grid, avoid empty corners and monotonous repeating texture. No labels, text, letters, numbers, logos, interface, borders, boxes, panels, people, patients, faces, cartoon characters. Never pretend this is an experimentally resolved molecular structure. Conceptual educational view. Deliver image only. Subject: a neuronal synapse viewed in clear cutaway, with an upper presynaptic terminal and lower postsynaptic cell separated by a broad extracellular synaptic cleft. Upper terminal occupies upper half; gently curved phospholipid membrane runs along y=50%. Several vesicles INSIDE upper terminal contain small amber neurotransmitter dots. At x=30%, blue voltage-gated calcium channel spans the membrane, with turquoise calcium spheres OUTSIDE in the cleft and a thin UPWARD arrow through channel bringing calcium INTO upper terminal. At x=65%, one amber-dot-filled vesicle fuses continuously with membrane in an omega shape and releases amber dots DOWNWARD into extracellular cleft. Arrows must distinguish calcium inward versus transmitter outward. Lower postsynaptic cell begins y=80%, its membrane has teal receptors facing UP into cleft; amber transmitter binds a receptor, no calcium channel on lower cell confused with presynaptic one. Mitochondrion upper-left, vesicles upper-right, distinct channel left-center, fusion site right-center, receptors lower third. Schematic shapes rendered with sophisticated soft dimension. Do NOT show extracellular calcium travelling outward from terminal. Do NOT show vesicles inside cleft or merge the cells. Diagram of normal calcium-coupled synaptic transmission; variant effects are not depicted.

Use case: scientific-educational. Edit this conceptual synapse illustration into a cleaner SCIENTIFIC EDITORIAL ILLUSTRATION for a professional genetics learning puzzle. Preserve the biological arrangement and correct directions. Landscape 4:3. Make it feel like a carefully art-directed modern journal explanatory figure: flat, matte shapes with very restrained soft depth, precise clean edges, smooth surfaces, selective details. NO glossy 3D render, NO molecular gravel or mottled texture, NO spiderweb filaments, NO background floating blobs, NO pseudo-atomic protein helices, NO blurry particles. Reduce complexity by about 70 percent. Background warm white. Upper presynaptic terminal pale periwinkle with an elegant dark-navy outline and two smooth membrane bands instead of hundreds of individual lipids. One simplified mitochondrion in upper-left, just three clearly spaced vesicles with sparse amber dots across upper-middle and upper-right. Large distinct navy calcium channel at left-center membrane, teal calcium circles OUTSIDE below membrane and a fine upward teal arrow through the channel INTO terminal. At right-center a clearly fused omega-shaped vesicle releasing six amber transmitter dots downward into cleft. Bottom: a pale teal postsynaptic membrane, three simple dark-teal receptors facing up, one amber transmitter bound to central receptor. Each object easy to identify at phone size. Make upper-left mitochondrion, upper-right vesicles, middle-left channel, middle-right release and bottom receptors strong independent jigsaw landmarks. Thin arrows only at calcium entry and transmitter release. No text, lettering, numeric markers, border, gene name, logo or UI. This is conceptual normal transmission, not an experimentally measured structure. The finished image should teach calcium entry then transmitter release at a glance and look refined, calm, and human-designed.
